gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns failure to establish a rational, polynomial-bit-size discrete reduction after spectral normalization and Cholesky factorization. ISSUE-005 diagnoses an inverted scaling substitution in a separate equivalence lemma; it does not identify rational encoding, bit complexity, or construction-time obligations for the reduction.

The gold issue is the missing nonpositive-objective hypothesis in the implication from local minimum to Nash pair. ISSUE-001 concerns overstating convergence to locally optimal points rather than critical points; it does not recognize the blockwise Nash implication or its omitted sign condition.

The gold issue is that arbitrary, non-orthonormal columns are treated as an orthogonal projector, invalidating the feasibility test. ISSUE-003 instead identifies division by zero when the spectral radius is zero and the missing positive-radius hypothesis; it does not recognize the normalization/projector defect.

The gold issue is the false spectral-radius identity when arbitrary basis vectors are not normalized. ISSUE-004 concerns omission of zero eigenvalues from an eigenvalue correspondence for a singular product; its correction does not identify the separate basis-normalization defect.

The gold issue is that the stated sphere-constrained block feasible sets are nonconvex, so the convex-block convergence theorem cannot justify the guarantee. ISSUE-001 identifies a mismatch between convergence to critical points and claims of local optimality, but does not diagnose the nonconvex sphere constraint or the missing convexity premise.
